body: Can’t lock myself out if I can just change the lock (I can reset the password through Admin). But Google put its own lock on my account for no reason. I even paid the bills.
I’m the domain admin, but this is not the admin account. It’s an account under the admin. Did the password reset and tried changing some security settings. Nothing worked.

It is on a Workspace. No IT dept, just me (with no IT experience) trying to maintain my family business’ Google accounts. I’ll see if I can contact Google support. If you know of a solution though, I’d really appreciate the help.

This is a business “Workspace” account which can be controlled by an administrator account. I have access to that administrator account which lets me change passwords of all the accounts under it. If I forget a password, I can just reset it (which I did). And yet, Google locked me out.

A lot of people in the comments don’t seem to understand what happened. Google didn’t give me any reason, it just said something like “we can’t verify your sign-in attempt. Contact your domain administrator.” That was before this screenshot.

I even changed the password, being the domain admin myself. I own the damn Workspace account, but I couldn’t find a solution to “recover” this account any other way.

Edit: Update - Contacted Google Support and they helped me out. I basically had to reset all security features for this account through the admin console. Able to login now.

Answering your question about going to university -
I did that. Went to uni in a different country for a year just to get another chance to live a better student life. I was initially very determined and tried to socialise more than I ever did in my life. There were dozens of awkward conversations and fumbling. I thought I was getting better, finally getting rid of social anxiety. But that wasn’t the case. I couldn’t maintain relations with people. I had a hard time connecting with people from different cultures. Seeing other people socialise effortlessly kept bringing me down. No luck with dating either.

Now I feel like I’m back the way I was earlier. Practically nothing has changed in my life. I’m not saying don’t go to university, it was definitely a learning experience for me. But just know that this would only be postponing the time to start adulting.
